title: Propitiation
definition: Propitiation is Christ's wrath-bearing sacrifice that satisfies God's holy justice and opens the way for mercy.
summary: Propitiation teaches that Christ's sacrifice satisfies God's righteous wrath against sin.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the sacrifice appointed by God, displaying both divine justice and saving love.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Propitiation addresses the holy anger of God against evil. In love, God provides His own Son as the sacrifice that turns away wrath from His people. This doctrine does not make the Father reluctant to love; it shows that divine love saves in a way that upholds holiness and justice.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because the Gospel becomes shallow when God's wrath is ignored. Propitiation shows why the cross was necessary and why forgiveness is more than sentiment. It helps believers tremble at sin and rejoice that judgment has been borne by Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Do not minimize sin as though wrath were an embarrassment to hide. Worship Christ as the sacrifice who bore what you deserved. Proclaim the cross as the place where holy justice and saving love meet.
